transcript.text: Good evening, everyone. We need to conduct our round-robin review of the tribute's broadcast operating plan before I can approve it. Let's go through this systematically -- technical, rights, talent, and safety. Who would like to start?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: During a broadcast line test this afternoon, I measured a 180-millisecond latency that makes a live instrumental feed unusable with the house video system. The tested workaround is a pre-recorded instrumental stem with live vocals, but I have not entered the result in the sign-off packet yet.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a rights issue. My written license confirmation, which I received today but haven't yet logged in the rights tracker, only permits a 45-second excerpt of the tribute recording. It forbids any replay after the broadcast, and requires the on-screen credit 'Music courtesy of Meridian Songs.' The current production plan calls for a 90-second song excerpt, which exceeds what we're cleared for by 45 seconds.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical talent issue. I confirmed with the lead performer's agent this morning that the lead can only appear remotely from 8:50 PM to 9:00 PM — not in person. The current production plan calls for an eight-minute in-person full-band performance, which is directly at odds with what the agent has approved. The agent's email is still awaiting entry on the talent calendar, which is why this hasn't surfaced in the sign-off materials yet.
transcript.speaker: A4

The post-rehearsal safety inspection found that confetti is prohibited beneath the theater's sprinkler array, and a clear audience aisle measuring exactly 1.5 meters is required. I received the inspection minutes after the draft plan circulated and have not yet amended that draft, so the current plan's confetti drop is in violation of safety requirements.
